A cave entrance has been spotted nearby. Send an expedition member to search for metal ore. A higher Patrolling skill and your own Scouting will increase the potential boon of exploring caves. Beware that caves can be dangerous, and there’s a risk that the follower may sustain a light injury.

Natives have been known to bury their dead nearby. Send an expedition member to search the graves for valuable trinkets. Unused Meat spoils overnight. You can convert Meat to Rations each night by using the Preserve task during Camp Management.
The Scout is a high damage melee unit with great movement range, good for flanking and hit-and-run tactics.
Soldiers have high defence and good melee attacks and are great for protecting your more fragile units.
Hunters are your best ranged units but very weak in melee combat.
Doctors are your basic healers, capable of restoring a measure of Endurance to other units during combat, or (on higher levels) curing negative effects and even reviving incapacitated allies.

The Scholar is a support unit who excels at making other units better and whose ranged attacks automatically lower an enemy’s Defence for all allies for the rest of the turn (regardless of whether or not it hits).

When available, use the Preparation phase to select a good starting formation and to place traps and barricades.

Auto-assigning tasks on the Camp Management screen is a convenience that does not necessarily give you the optimal outcome. Remember to double-check your tasks after using it!
Contextual events such as fishing are a great way to gain extra resources when you make camp.
Remember to spend some time exploring the world for optional quests and events that can give you more resources and experience points.
High morale not only prevents your units from leaving you in a mutiny, it also improves their critical hit chance in combat.

Cristoforo Colombo was the Italian explorer who discovered the Americas. Though he suffered some setbacks, his expeditions were quite successful. If you pick this setting, you are most likely to be successful as well.

Personality traits determine which decisions and events will cause each follower to gain or lose Morale.

*Aggressive*
May gain morale when you engage an enemy in combat, but may lose morale if you pass up an opportunity to fight.

*Peaceful*
May gain morale when you manage to avoid combat, but may lose morale if you deliberately seek out battle.

*Racist*
May lose morale if you recruit followers of another ethnicity, but may gain morale if you display racism.

*Open-Minded*
May gain morale if you recruit followers of another ethnicity, but may lose morale if you display racism.

*Greedy*
May gain morale if you gain new resources, but may in turn lose morale if you give up or lose resources.

*Altruistic*
May gain morale if you give up your resources for a good cause, but may lose morale if you behave greedily.

*Courageous*
May gain morale if you stand your ground against a superior force, but may lose morale if you retreat from a dangerous situation.

*Cautious*
May gain morale if you avoid dangerous situations, but may lose morale if you take unnecessary risks.

*Narcissistic*
May gain morale if chosen for a task or promoted to a higher rank, but may lose morale if passed over for promotion.

*Proud*
Gains morale every time you win a battle, but loses morale if you are defeated or fail to accomplish your goals.

*Pious*
May gain morale if you act in accordance with their faith, but may lose morale if you transgress against their religious creed.

*Adventurous*
May gain morale every time you make a significant discovery, but may lose morale if you shy away from adventure.

*Lovesick*
Is in love with another follower. Will gain morale if you promote their lover but lose morale if their lover dies.

*Rivalrous*
Has developed a rivalry with another follower. Will lose morale if you promote their ribval but gain it if their rival dies.

*Traumatised*
Has had their spirit broken due to a traumatic experience.

*Treacherous*
Has demonstrated an disconcerting lack of loyalty to your leadership.

*Married*
Will gain morale if you demonstrate fidelity but lose morale if you flirt with others.

Guide

Welcome to Character Creation. This is where you choose what kind of Conquistador you wish to be. Your choices in this menu and the following will influence your opportunities and challenges throughout the game. But don't be alarmed! The decisions you make here may make the game harder, but they cannot make it impossible.

The current screen lets you set up your own character - gender, name, and skills. Your skills will influence your access to, and consumption of, resources such as medicine and rations, and skills will also open up new options during events and conversations.

You can always move your cursor over icons to see what they mean.

It is recommended that you choose two or three skills to specialise in, without lowering any of your skills completely - but feel free to follow your instincts if they tell you otherwise.

On the next screen, you will have to select the people to bring on your expedition to the New World. The different character types provide substantial bonuses to your skills, and different characters have different strengths, weaknesses, and abilities in a battle.

Each character also has three personality traits which determine what will cause them to lose or gain morale throughout your travels.

Some Background

The year is 1518 - a year before Hernán Cortes would be elected captain of the third expedition to the South American mainland, where he would overthrow the Aztec empire. But that will not happen, because you have beaten him to the punch.

You are the eldest child of a Spanish nobleman, and you yourself hold the title of Hidalgo. With your father's backing, you have been the leader of a successful "hermandad" (meaning "brotherhood") back in the Old World - a peacekeeping association of armed individuals which protected the countryside around your father's town.

During this time, you demonstrated an aptitude for leadership and strategy that earned you the respect of the people under your command - but it was time for a greater challenge. With the King's permission and your father's financial support, you purchased a ship and selected your crew from the best of the brothers and sisters in your hermandad.

Together, you are off on the long and arduous journey to explore the New World. In your cargo hold, you bring rations, medicine, equipment, and assorted valuables. You must first make a stop on the Caribbean island of Hispaniola, under Spanish domain since 1496. Here, you will hire servants or buy slaves, rest and restock, and gain what information you can about the New World.

After five weeks on the Atlantic Ocean, your people gather on the deck as the call "Land ahoy!" rings out from the rigging. On a clear afternoon, gulls screeching in the wake of your ship, you sail into the port of Santo Domingo, the seat of Spanish colonial rule in the New World.

Born in 1469, he had a relatively normal childhood, growing up in a small farm town. He met the love of his life, whom he married at a young age. He was apprenticing as an alchemist when his wife fell ill from typhus and died a short while later. The loss sent him into a deep depression and he buried himself in his work and the field of disease treatment. He never fully recovered from his broken heart, and partly the reason he joined your expedition was to get over his grief. A somber and quiet man, but no man knows better the field of diseases and infections than he.

Born in 1487 into a family of healers, her father a doctor and her mother a herbalist. Throughout her childhood she exhibited a cynical and brutal outlook, seeing the human body as nothing more than flesh which can be repaired like anything else. Her dispassion and cynicism are troubling, but her skills are flawless and unmatched.

Teresa's mother died when she was giving birth, launching her father into a deep depression from which he never recovered. Seeing suffering all around her as a child, she grew determined to help people get well. Before joining your expedition, she was the local doctor in your area, where she excelled particularly in stitching wounds.

Not much is known about Antonio, beside him being an extremely talented doctor. How he gained the knowledge he possesses or the skills that he exhibits are a mystery. Wandering into town from the forest on a day like any other, he quickly attracted a crowd of curious people in the poor quarters. He went from person to person and, with simple remedies, made almost every sick person better. His sympathetic nature is unmatched and he can make any person feel welcome in his company.

Born in servitude to your family, Sierra started her training as a squire. She developed a taste for combat very quickly and her skills became apparent to you. At your suggestion she joined your hermandad as a full-time soldier, and has been training there for the past several years before you went on your expedition.

Born into a family of brawlers and troublemakers, Alberto was no different. He frequently ran into trouble as a child and got his fair share of scars to prove it. Before joining your hermandad, he worked as a barkeep in a less-than-reputable establishment, where his skills in fighting were put to good use. He eventually tired of the stink and joined you, in hopes of fresh air and fresh enemies.

Born as a street urchin to unknown parents, she spent her childhood stealing to survive. On a particularly sunny day she ran into your father, who took pity on the small child. Her fearlessness and tenacious will to live made her a prime candidate for your army, in which she has now spent the last seven years waiting for a chance to repay her debt to your father through service.

Born in 1493 and a distant relative on your mother's side. She became noticed for hunting down a group of local bandits near her home and singlehandedly disposing of them. Her feat was more through blind luck than talent, but through training with your hermandad, she became a skilled and remarkable fighter.

Not much is known of Juan Ortega. Despite his ruthlessness on the field of battle, he is a polite and soft-spoken character most of the time, but he keeps to himself and doesn't speak of his past. It has been established that he served as a mercenary for a few years before travelling to Hispaniola where he joined your expedition, but nobody knows where he is from or why he chose to come to the New World. With every passing evening, the rumours concerning "Maestro" Ortega grow ever more impressive.

Young Rosalía is the daughter to your father's most trusted sword-arm. From the time she could walk, she started her training, her father determined to honour his name. Because her father had wished for a son, approval did not come easy, but she attained it. Her loyalty is unquestionable and despite her youth, her swordsmanship is flawless.

Born in 1494 on a farm on the outskirts of your fiefdom, she lost her parents to robber knights, who raided and destroyed her childhood home. Vowing her revenge, she joined your hermandad as a soldier to kill those who murdered her parents. Her revenge was eventually achieved, after which she assumed a much more calm demeanor. Her skills in combat are almost unrivaled, which is the reason she chose to stay in your service.

Guillermo Pascual was already experienced in combat at the age of 19, having fought in countless skirmishes and battles. Born into your mother's service, his family has acted as a personal militia to her family for generations. He joined your hermandad as a sergeant and helped train others while honing his own skills. Guillermo is stubborn and ruthless, yet you would be hard pressed to find a better man to bring into the fray.

Born in 1485 and a distant relative on your mother's side, a Hidalgo in his own right, he was persuaded to join your hermandad at the age of 19. It was hoped that his time with you would teach him some lessons in humility, but it quickly became apparent that his temper was uncontrollable. In combat, however, his temper is channeled and focused, making him an invaluable asset.

Born in 1494 to a blacksmith in Madrid, where at a young age he began his life as an apprentice. At the age of 15 he began his training as a soldier under your banner. He showed a ferocity and zeal that made him stand out from the others and proved his worth as a soldier of your hermandad.

Blanca's father gave her to a nunnery at a young age, as her family could not afford to get her married. The nuns provided a harsh but stimulating childhood with a remarkably broad and scholarly educational regimen which instilled in her a love of knowledge and intellectual pursuit. When she came of age, Blanca joined a mission to Hispaniola where she helped to establish a new church on the north coast. When the opportunity arose, she jumped at the chance to follow you to the mainland and bring the word of God to the natives.

Daniel Reyes grew up in a family of soldiers, and he was determined to ascend from the family tradition. Though his father set him on the path of a military career, he chose to study strategy and battle tactics, and through hard work and stubbornness he earned a respectable place as a war advisor to a Marquis. But Reyes is in possession of an ever travelling mind, and when rumours from the New World reached his ears, speaking of dark cults and heathen rituals, he set his sights on those mysterious new shores. If there was ancient magic and forbidden knowledge there, it would be his.

Julio's father was killed defending his birthing mother. His parents had been travelling to your town when they were attacked by bandits. His mother escaped, wounded and breaking water. She collapsed and died close to the city gates, but luckily a young couple rescued Julio from his dying mother's womb and raised the child as their own. Because his adoptive father was the keeper of your father's library, Julio grew up surrounded by books and pamphlets alike. It was natural for him to turn to the sciences in that environment. Yet something stirred in him, driving him to seek adventure.

Mercedes was born in 1496 to unknown parents. She was found on the steps at a convent where she was taken in and cared for. Growing up, she proved extremely difficult for the nuns, preferring to study fields that challenged their faith. In fear of being branded a witch, she ran away at age 13 and lived a secluded life up until joining your expedition. Her insights into mythology are unrivaled, and facing a world with a rich mythology in its own right, she is an invaluable asset.

Zárraga is a hunter of knowledge, ruthless in his approach. No books or scrolls are unavailable to him, as any who tries to keep them from him is dragged through defamation to the verge of bankruptcy. The means always justify the end for Carlos Zárraga, and the lore and secrets of the new world WILL be revealed to him, even if it means torturing every soul he finds.

Beautiful Bonita was the daughter of a royal huntsman to the King. Her radiant charms and her incredible beauty made her the most attractive maiden in the court, to the extent that her father was forced to hire guards to keep the suitors away. What most women would kill to have was a curse to Bonita, however, as she longed to be respected and admired for her achievements rather than her looks. This desire finally drove her to run away and join your expedition.

Besides the year of his birth, not much is known about the past of Raúl Carrillo. For years, he was a wanted man, accused of poaching and other inappropriate activities. How he managed to escape the law for so long is unknown, but his continued freedom is a testament to his talents. He is ill-tempered and quick to anger, but in the jungles his patience knows no bounds. For hours on end he can be still, ready to pounce at the blink of an eye.

Born in 1489, she grew up in the city under the roof of a fletcher. Her knowledge of bows rivals any expert, and her ability to handle them exceeds even that, but she's proven to be equally handy with an arquebus. She trained with the city guard for several years, before eventually surpassing her superiors, taking over their duties in teaching her fellow students. Although not exactly humble, she is still well aware of her limitations and has an overall pleasant personality, making her a great companion.

Rafael had a good life as a hunter in Spain, until he messed it all up. Blind with baseless jealousy and drunk out of his mind, he murdered his loving wife one night on suspicion of adultery. He was caught and tried for murder, found guilty and sentenced to death. At the last possible moment, Rafael was offered a chance of pardon if he agreed to be sent to the New World and serve the Spanish Crown on expeditions to the mainland.

Alejandro was the son of a Vizconde whose house fell into disgrace and destitution when he ran afoul of a cardinal and became a target of the Inquisition. The nature and origin of the dispute that felled Pintado are murky and mysterious, and if Alejandro knows anything, he isn't willing to share it. He joined your hermandad hoping to restore honour to his name, and so far he's been doing quite well.

Life was not good to Gabriela in the early years of her life. Thrown out of her family's house to fend for herself at the age of 12, she resorted to prostitution and begging to feed herself. After she nearly died following a desperate makeshift abortion, her luck finally changed when she was taken in by a lonely old woodsman who taught her hunting and tanning. Her sense of self-worth finally restored after several years of maintaining a respectable living, she joined the crew of a ship to Hispaniola, where you met her as a hunter in the forests northeast of Santo Domingo.

Ever since he was a child, Montego always had a strong sense of civic duty and a powerful desire to find adventure and be a hero, but he was never very good at combat or very fond of killing people. When he joined your hermandad, he took up the study of maps and orienteering and quickly became the best scout in your brotherhood. As long as Montego is with you, you know that you will never get lost.

Francisco is a short and slender young man with delicate features and a rogueish charm. Though he had only recently joined your hermandad by the time you left for the New World, he was eager to join your expedition. What he lacks in strength, he more than makes up for in endurance and agility, and his acrobatic tricks are particularly popular in the evening around the campfires.

Daniela was a farmer's daughter who married a wealthy merchant relatively late, at the age of 15. The couple travelled a lot, and Daniela quickly learned how to survive on the road, in many types of terrain and weather. Her natural talent for path finding served her husband well, and for several years, business was good. When Daniela was in her mid-20s, tragedy struck as her husband was murdered by a business partner and robbed of all his possessions. Left a destitute widow, Daniela was found and taken in by a member of your hermandad, where she put her skills to good use.

Born in 1498, Raina is a stoic and professional-minded woman who joined your hermandad at an early age hoping to find a place where she could feel like she belonged. She prefers subtlety and cleverness over force and confrontation, and she possesses a seemingly endless font of tricks and knowledge of wilderness survival.

The oldest person in your expedition, Federico has many years of active service experience as a soldier, but has always been too insubordinate to advance beyond a basic rank. When he offered to join your expedition, you suspected that the very qualities that made him a poor soldier - his independence and his utter lack of honour - would make him an excellent scout, and indeed Federico has since proven himself to be highly resourceful and effective in his new role.

Fierce and independent Ana picked up the nickname "Pantera" among the troops early in the expedition. When on duty, she is remarkable for her ability to move unnoticed through any terrain, like a shadow that leaves no mark upon its surroundings. Needless to say, this makes her an excellent scout. Off duty, she is remarkable for having several lovers and not even attempting to conceal her conduct. Naturally, this gives rise to all sorts of gossipping, jealousy, and contempt among the troops, but Anita herself seems perfectly disinterested in all this.
Alcazar de Colon

Juan Noriega is acting Governor while Santo Domingo is recovering from Leandra's attack. Perhaps he will be elected permanently into the position once everything is back to normal, but you don't really plan to stick around long enough to find out.
The palace is no different with Leandra in charge. Even most of the staff seems to be the same staff that De Manzanedo employed, and they still won't let you in without good reason.

For once, the Governor's staff is happy to let you directly into his office even though you have no good reason. He offers you a glass of wine and asks if there's anything he can do for you, but he's already done everything that he can do. After what you've done for Santo Domingo, he's all too happy to let you mount your expedition as soon as you're ready.

Governor Bernardo De Manzanedo's staff doesn't even attempt to stop you this time, so obvious is the urgency you exude. You find the Governor in his office with Juan Noriega, poring over defensive plans of the town. He looks up at you with alarm as you enter.
"What is it?"
"Leandra is coming to attack the city with all her troops, we must prepare the defenses forthwith."
"Is Esteban coming as well?"
"Esteban is dead, he will trouble you no longer."
The Governor claps his hands together and makes a small and rather silly leap into the air. Noriega smiles, but it's a sad smile.
"Well done! Well done indeed! You finally did it, what none of us could achieve. You brought down the giant!"
"On the contrary, Esteban is on our side now - he fights under my command."
Noriega and the Governor stare at you in astonished silence, as though you just told them that in fact it is the Earth that orbits the Sun, and not the other way around.
"That is the most preposterous thing I have heard in my entire life. What could you possibly have promised Esteban to make him join your company?"
"A harsh and dangerous life of adventure on the mainland. That's what he was fighting for all along."
"Well... if anyone can keep Esteban in check, perhaps that person is you. I suppose his loyalties will be put to the test if Leandra really is attacking Santo Domingo as soon as you say."
"Esteban is beaten. I spared his life, but he will trouble you no further, I assure you."
Noriega looks bewildered, you're not sure De Manzanedo has been keeping him in the loop. The governor frowns.
"I would prefer that you had killed Esteban, God knows his crimes merit it. However, if you say that he will not return to haunt us again, I will take your word for it."
As if on cue, a horn blares across the tense calm of the courtyard below. Noriega draws his sword and grits his teeth.
"The alarm signal! /She's here./"
Continue.

The Governor runs to the balcony and looks out across the town. Gunshots go off in the distance and chaos engulfs the courtyard as it fills with panicked servants and armed troops. Capitán Noriega puts a hand on your shoulder.

"This is it. I'm sorry we've held you here this long PSenorSenorita PNameLast, but we need your help one last time. The rebels will focus their attack on two locations: Alcazar de Colon and Fortaleza Ozama. My company will hold the fortress, your troops must rally here and protect the Governor. Go to the courtyard and prepare your defenses. May the Lord watch over you."
"May He watch over us all."
"Good luck, Juan. Watch your back."
Salute and hurry off.

You run through the fancy corridors of the palace, brushing through servants and staff members, flying down the stairs, and making a beeline for the courtyard. Your troops are already waiting for you outside, weapons at the ready. Isabela steps out in front of the rest.

"Capitán, Noriega's troops are heading out to the fortress, but they are too few - they will not be able to cover all the entry points. I request permission to take a few of the troops over there and reinforce Noriega's position."
"No, I need you here."
"Capitán PNameLast, I fear for Umberto's safety! Let me go and help to protect the fortress!"
"Very well, go and make sure that Umberto is safe. But take care of yourself, Isabela!"
"I said no! I cannot spare you!"
She clenches her fists, stepping back into the line.
"Si, Capitán."
"Granted, but watch yourself over there."
Isabela jumps forward and gives you a strong hug.
"I will! And you too, PNameFirst. Good luck!"

You run through the fancy corridors of the palace, brushing through servants and staff members, flying down the stairs, and making a beeline for the courtyard. Your troops are already waiting for you outside, weapons at the ready. FNameFirst1 steps out in front of the rest.
"We're ready, Capitán! Awaiting your command."
"/Compañía Atencion/."
Everybody stands at attention all at once, and as the last civilians scurry across the courtyard and out of sight, an eerie silence falls over your immediate surroundings.

"We did not come here to fight a war. We did not come here to put our lives on the line for the sake of others. We did not come here to kill our fellow Spaniards. But we will do all of these things, because it is required of us on this day."

"None of us expected to find ourselves here on this day, defending a town and an island where we are merely visitors. But this is not a strange and foreign land. This town /is Spain/. It is a small corner of our home, lovingly recreated upon these beautiful shores. This is /worth/ defending."
The troops are staring straight ahead, but you can tell that they're listening intently to every word out of your mouth.

"Hispaniola is our harbour, our haven - the final stepping stone on our path to the mainland. If we are to conquer the New World, we must first prove that we are capable of holding on to what we've conquered already."

"The people here are honest men and women, Spaniards with strong hearts who have heard the siren song of the unexplored and dangerous New World - exactly as we have. These brave settlers have called upon us to aid them in facing a ruthless and unexpected enemy. We /must/ answer this call."
A few of your people can't help but nod stoically.

"The rebels will come at us with all they've got. They believe they have righteous cause, and that justice is on their side, but we know the truth - they are driven by greed and conceit! Stand fast and stand together, and we will show these marauders what /true righteousness/ can achieve!"

"Our enemies aim to destroy us, and to take the lives of all these innocent people who have blessed us with their hospitality and their friendship since we first set foot on this island. This is our chance to pay them back, and to quell the fires of rebellion /once and for all!/"
"This is not a time for great speeches - it is a time to seize your weapons and fight for your lives. Watch each other's backs and kill your enemies, and we will triumph today. Good luck to you all."
Your troops raise their swords in salute and shout with one voice.
"Por la gloria!"

Your ranks disperse across the courtyard, taking up their positions behind the carts and barricades Noriega's people set up to slow down the enemy. An aeon seems to pass in anxious anticipation. Then, a mish-mash of Spanish soldiers and Taíno warriors sidle out between the buildings, bearing down on the palace. You're vaguely aware of the sound of shutters being closed above you as Bernardo de Manzanedo takes cover inside his walls.
Begin the battle.

Somehow, you manage to beat back the enemies. It feels like you fight for an eternity, and your troops are exhausted, but as you watch the surviving rebels scatter back out into the town with their tails between their legs, you all muster enough energy for an enthusiastic cheer. One of your people brings you a bag of caltrops from a dead rebel. The Governor hazards leaving his palace and shuffles out the front door to have a word with you.
Continue.

"That was incredible, PNameLast. I see that I grossly underestimated your tactical proficiency. You and your men have saved my life, I know that, but if you have any fight left in you, I beseech you to move out and see how the fight is going in the other parts of the town."
"I need to check on Noriega in the fortress. I will return when I have news."
"What about you, if we leave you here, will you be safe?"
He nods reassuringly.

"They've given up their attempt to take the palace for now - if we can keep pushing them in the other parts of town, they won't be able to regroup for another proper attempt, and my personal guards can easily handle any stragglers or opportunists that return to exploit your absence."
"Very well, good luck Governor."
"All right, go back inside. I will see how things look closer to the fortress."
The Governor nods and then hurries back inside.
Defend Santo Domingo
You've beaten back the rebel assault on the palace. You should find out how things look in the other parts of the town.

The rebels eventually overwhelm your initial lines and push through your troops. You're manoeuvred to the side, cut off from the palace, and held at bay while the rebels storm the palace. Your desperate attempts to break the deadlock and come to the Governor's rescue are thwarted, and moments later Bernardo de Manzanedo's body comes crashing out of a window on the second floor and plummets to the ground. It's clear that the palace is lost, and you're forced to withdraw your troops back into the town.

As expected, the Governor's staff will not let you into his office unless you've got something important to report.

The Governor's staff leads you to his office again, though you could easily find your way by now. The Governor expectantly waits for you to speak.
"I have confronted Esteban in the mines and killed his men, but I was too late to prevent them from killing the troops."
De Manzanedo makes a pained grimace.
"And the brute himself? Is he dead?"
"He escaped, Governor, and you would not believe how if you didn't see it with your own eyes."
The Governor sits down with a sigh.
"So he eludes us again. Unbelievable. You are not the first to fail, PNameLast. I wonder if we shall ever stop that man."
"Is there any news about Leandra?"
He shakes his head.

"You are free to explore Hispaniola while we wait for Leandra to make her move, but despite the service you have already done us, I cannot in good conscience let your company leave this island until the threat from Leandra has been dealt with."
"So I must sit here and twiddle my thumbs until the rebels attack?"

"It would serve us better to have some knowledge of the rebel movements on the island. I invite you to go out and search for more information while we wait - see if we can get out in front of this and achieve the upper hand for once."
The Governor curtly calls his servants in to show you to the door.
"I understand. It doesn't please me, but I will remain here and help to protect Santo Domingo."
"Thank you, PNameLast. You have shown yourself to be a good ally in this conflict. Good luck."
"There is more, Governor."
In blatant defiance of the common restrictions on human physiognomy, the Governor's face falls even further.
"I have also visited San Tiago and seen Leandra Vizcaino. It was a trap! /She/ is the leader of the north coast rebels!"
"He will resurface - a man like Esteban cannot stay out of sight for long."

"You are right of course - and now you know what kind of creature you're facing. Next time, make sure to be better prepared. Meanwhile, you should pursue the other lead, talk to Capitán Vizcaino about the north coast rebels."
"I'm getting to that."
The Governor nods curtly and calls his servants in to show you to the door.

On the way out, you pass Capitán Noriega in the hall.

"Oh, PNameLast. I'd been meaning to talk to you. Umberto and his people have been clearing out the city guard's old training grounds outside the city, we're ready to arrange that tournament whenever you're ready."
"Great, I'll drop by Fortaleza Ozama when I'm ready."

Born in 1469, he had a relatively normal childhood, growing up in a small farm town. He met the love of his life, whom he married at a young age. He was apprenticing as an alchemist when his wife fell ill from typhus and died a short while later. The loss sent him into a deep depression and he buried himself in his work and the field of disease treatment. He never fully recovered from his broken heart, and partly the reason he joined your expedition was to get over his grief. A somber and quiet man, but no man knows better the field of diseases and infections than he.

Born in 1487 into a family of healers, her father a doctor and her mother a herbalist. Throughout her childhood she exhibited a cynical and brutal outlook, seeing the human body as nothing more than flesh which can be repaired like anything else. Her dispassion and cynicism are troubling, but her skills are flawless and unmatched.

Teresa's mother died when she was giving birth, launching her father into a deep depression from which he never recovered. Seeing suffering all around her as a child, she grew determined to help people get well. Before joining your expedition, she was the local doctor in your area, where she excelled particularly in stitching wounds.

Not much is known about Antonio, beside him being an extremely talented doctor. How he gained the knowledge he possesses or the skills that he exhibits are a mystery. Wandering into town from the forest on a day like any other, he quickly attracted a crowd of curious people in the poor quarters. He went from person to person and, with simple remedies, made almost every sick person better. His sympathetic nature is unmatched and he can make any person feel welcome in his company.

Born in servitude to your family, Sierra started her training as a squire. She developed a taste for combat very quickly and her skills became apparent to you. At your suggestion she joined your hermandad as a full-time soldier, and has been training there for the past several years before you went on your expedition.

Born into a family of brawlers and troublemakers, Alberto was no different. He frequently ran into trouble as a child and got his fair share of scars to prove it. Before joining your hermandad, he worked as a barkeep in a less-than-reputable establishment, where his skills in fighting were put to good use. He eventually tired of the stink and joined you, in hopes of fresh air and fresh enemies.

Born as a street urchin to unknown parents, she spent her childhood stealing to survive. On a particularly sunny day she ran into your father, who took pity on the small child. Her fearlessness and tenacious will to live made her a prime candidate for your army, in which she has now spent the last seven years waiting for a chance to repay her debt to your father through service.

Born in 1493 and a distant relative on your mother's side. She became noticed for hunting down a group of local bandits near her home and singlehandedly disposing of them. Her feat was more through blind luck than talent, but through training with your hermandad, she became a skilled and remarkable fighter.

Not much is known of Juan Ortega. Despite his ruthlessness on the field of battle, he is a polite and soft-spoken character most of the time, but he keeps to himself and doesn't speak of his past. It has been established that he served as a mercenary for a few years before travelling to Hispaniola where he joined your expedition, but nobody knows where he is from or why he chose to come to the New World. With every passing evening, the rumours concerning "Maestro" Ortega grow ever more impressive.

Young Rosalía is the daughter to your father's most trusted sword-arm. From the time she could walk, she started her training, her father determined to honour his name. Because her father had wished for a son, approval did not come easy, but she attained it. Her loyalty is unquestionable and despite her youth, her swordsmanship is flawless.

Born in 1494 on a farm on the outskirts of your fiefdom, she lost her parents to robber knights, who raided and destroyed her childhood home. Vowing her revenge, she joined your hermandad as a soldier to kill those who murdered her parents. Her revenge was eventually achieved, after which she assumed a much more calm demeanor. Her skills in combat are almost unrivaled, which is the reason she chose to stay in your service.

Guillermo Pascual was already experienced in combat at the age of 19, having fought in countless skirmishes and battles. Born into your mother's service, his family has acted as a personal militia to her family for generations. He joined your hermandad as a sergeant and helped train others while honing his own skills. Guillermo is stubborn and ruthless, yet you would be hard pressed to find a better man to bring into the fray.

Born in 1485 and a distant relative on your mother's side, a Hidalgo in his own right, he was persuaded to join your hermandad at the age of 19. It was hoped that his time with you would teach him some lessons in humility, but it quickly became apparent that his temper was uncontrollable. In combat, however, his temper is channeled and focused, making him an invaluable asset.

Born in 1494 to a blacksmith in Madrid, where at a young age he began his life as an apprentice. At the age of 15 he began his training as a soldier under your banner. He showed a ferocity and zeal that made him stand out from the others and proved his worth as a soldier of your hermandad.

Blanca's father gave her to a nunnery at a young age, as her family could not afford to get her married. The nuns provided a harsh but stimulating childhood with a remarkably broad and scholarly educational regimen which instilled in her a love of knowledge and intellectual pursuit. When she came of age, Blanca joined a mission to Hispaniola where she helped to establish a new church on the north coast. When the opportunity arose, she jumped at the chance to follow you to the mainland and bring the word of God to the natives.

Daniel Reyes grew up in a family of soldiers, and he was determined to ascend from the family tradition. Though his father set him on the path of a military career, he chose to study strategy and battle tactics, and through hard work and stubbornness he earned a respectable place as a war advisor to a Marquis. But Reyes is in possession of an ever travelling mind, and when rumours from the New World reached his ears, speaking of dark cults and heathen rituals, he set his sights on those mysterious new shores. If there was ancient magic and forbidden knowledge there, it would be his.

Julio's father was killed defending his birthing mother. His parents had been travelling to your town when they were attacked by bandits. His mother escaped, wounded and breaking water. She collapsed and died close to the city gates, but luckily a young couple rescued Julio from his dying mother's womb and raised the child as their own. Because his adoptive father was the keeper of your father's library, Julio grew up surrounded by books and pamphlets alike. It was natural for him to turn to the sciences in that environment. Yet something stirred in him, driving him to seek adventure.

Mercedes was born in 1496 to unknown parents. She was found on the steps at a convent where she was taken in and cared for. Growing up, she proved extremely difficult for the nuns, preferring to study fields that challenged their faith. In fear of being branded a witch, she ran away at age 13 and lived a secluded life up until joining your expedition. Her insights into mythology are unrivaled, and facing a world with a rich mythology in its own right, she is an invaluable asset.

Zárraga is a hunter of knowledge, ruthless in his approach. No books or scrolls are unavailable to him, as any who tries to keep them from him is dragged through defamation to the verge of bankruptcy. The means always justify the end for Carlos Zárraga, and the lore and secrets of the new world WILL be revealed to him, even if it means torturing every soul he finds.

Beautiful Bonita was the daughter of a royal huntsman to the King. Her radiant charms and her incredible beauty made her the most attractive maiden in the court, to the extent that her father was forced to hire guards to keep the suitors away. What most women would kill to have was a curse to Bonita, however, as she longed to be respected and admired for her achievements rather than her looks. This desire finally drove her to run away and join your expedition.

Besides the year of his birth, not much is known about the past of Raúl Carrillo. For years, he was a wanted man, accused of poaching and other inappropriate activities. How he managed to escape the law for so long is unknown, but his continued freedom is a testament to his talents. He is ill-tempered and quick to anger, but in the jungles his patience knows no bounds. For hours on end he can be still, ready to pounce at the blink of an eye.

Born in 1489, she grew up in the city under the roof of a fletcher. Her knowledge of bows rivals any expert, and her ability to handle them exceeds even that, but she's proven to be equally handy with an arquebus. She trained with the city guard for several years, before eventually surpassing her superiors, taking over their duties in teaching her fellow students. Although not exactly humble, she is still well aware of her limitations and has an overall pleasant personality, making her a great companion.

Rafael had a good life as a hunter in Spain, until he messed it all up. Blind with baseless jealousy and drunk out of his mind, he murdered his loving wife one night on suspicion of adultery. He was caught and tried for murder, found guilty and sentenced to death. At the last possible moment, Rafael was offered a chance of pardon if he agreed to be sent to the New World and serve the Spanish Crown on expeditions to the mainland.

Alejandro was the son of a Vizconde whose house fell into disgrace and destitution when he ran afoul of a cardinal and became a target of the Inquisition. The nature and origin of the dispute that felled Pintado are murky and mysterious, and if Alejandro knows anything, he isn't willing to share it. He joined your hermandad hoping to restore honour to his name, and so far he's been doing quite well.

Life was not good to Gabriela in the early years of her life. Thrown out of her family's house to fend for herself at the age of 12, she resorted to prostitution and begging to feed herself. After she nearly died following a desperate makeshift abortion, her luck finally changed when she was taken in by a lonely old woodsman who taught her hunting and tanning. Her sense of self-worth finally restored after several years of maintaining a respectable living, she joined the crew of a ship to Hispaniola, where you met her as a hunter in the forests northeast of Santo Domingo.

Ever since he was a child, Montego always had a strong sense of civic duty and a powerful desire to find adventure and be a hero, but he was never very good at combat or very fond of killing people. When he joined your hermandad, he took up the study of maps and orienteering and quickly became the best scout in your brotherhood. As long as Montego is with you, you know that you will never get lost.

Francisco is a short and slender young man with delicate features and a rogueish charm. Though he had only recently joined your hermandad by the time you left for the New World, he was eager to join your expedition. What he lacks in strength, he more than makes up for in endurance and agility, and his acrobatic tricks are particularly popular in the evening around the campfires.

Daniela was a farmer's daughter who married a wealthy merchant relatively late, at the age of 15. The couple travelled a lot, and Daniela quickly learned how to survive on the road, in many types of terrain and weather. Her natural talent for path finding served her husband well, and for several years, business was good. When Daniela was in her mid-20s, tragedy struck as her husband was murdered by a business partner and robbed of all his possessions. Left a destitute widow, Daniela was found and taken in by a member of your hermandad, where she put her skills to good use.

Born in 1498, Raina is a stoic and professional-minded woman who joined your hermandad at an early age hoping to find a place where she could feel like she belonged. She prefers subtlety and cleverness over force and confrontation, and she possesses a seemingly endless font of tricks and knowledge of wilderness survival.

The oldest person in your expedition, Federico has many years of active service experience as a soldier, but has always been too insubordinate to advance beyond a basic rank. When he offered to join your expedition, you suspected that the very qualities that made him a poor soldier - his independence and his utter lack of honour - would make him an excellent scout, and indeed Federico has since proven himself to be highly resourceful and effective in his new role.

Fierce and independent Ana picked up the nickname "Pantera" among the troops early in the expedition. When on duty, she is remarkable for her ability to move unnoticed through any terrain, like a shadow that leaves no mark upon its surroundings. Needless to say, this makes her an excellent scout. Off duty, she is remarkable for having several lovers and not even attempting to conceal her conduct. Naturally, this gives rise to all sorts of gossipping, jealousy, and contempt among the troops, but Anita herself seems perfectly disinterested in all this.

The daughter of Andres de Yruenes, who was a part of Columbus' crew. Isabela's mother was a Taíno woman, and as a child of two worlds, Isabela has never found it easy to fit in. Despite her difficulties in gaining the trust of her mother's tribesmen, and the often terrible treatment she sustained from the colonists in Santo Domingo, Isabela has stubbornly held on to a positive outlook on life. She is far from naive, having seen many of the worst sides of people, but she is a stoically polite and open-minded woman who fights for peace and reconciliation for both her peoples.

Esteban came to Hispaniola at the age of 23. He was drafted into the army and served uneasily under Capitán Noriega for two years. When he was fed up, he deserted and lived by himself in the jungle for almost a decade. Eventually he joined a band of fellow deserters under the secret command of Leandra Vizcaino, but he soon took charge of the troops, and they became far more loyal to him. Fearing a power-struggle, Leandra ambushed his troops, driving Esteban to seek an alliance with the savage Caribs. There, you found him again, defeated him one last time, and convinced him to join you.

The Hungarian mercenary is a powerfully built man who looks particularly imposing in his black piecemeal armour. He was trained in Hungary's Black Army and fought against the Turks as well as a peasant rebellion. After the dissolution of the Fekete sereg, his company struck out on their own and he travelled to Italy to fight as a mercenary. Now he has come to the New World searching for his old friend, Tamás Szász.

Your people form up and move into the small farming community, doing their best to herd the terrified peasants together so they have nowhere to run. When the farmers finally realise what you're doing, they make a brave attempt to break through your ranks and escape into the fields.
Begin "battle".

What follows is an absolute massacre. Being simple farmers, and having nothing but crude farm tools at hand, the farmers don't stand a chance. Within minutes, all of them are fertilising the ground with their blood.

Your men put their best effort towards killing the peasants, but you can't prevent some of them from getting away. You quickly set about torching the farms while you keep an eye out for enemy reinforcements.
"Burn the farms but let the peasants go - and be ready for a counter-attack!"

Your people form up and move into the small farming community, setting fire to the homes and firing their arquebuses into the air to scare away the peasants. The farmers scatter in terror and flee into the fields.
Continue.

When all the farms are ablaze and the fire is beginning to spread to the crops, a group of Aztec warriors finally arrive from the countryside, led by an Eagle Warrior. Your troops spot them coming and have plenty of time to regroup and prepare for combat.
Begin battle.
Even though the Aztecs are well trained and well equipped, you manage to outsmart them and lead your troops to victory.
Continue.
Raze The Farms
Return to Xalapa and inform Tepictoton that Tenochtitlan will be receiving no supplies from the northern farms any longer.
Your people scavenge what they can off the corpses and wagons. Before you leave, you bury the people who were shot in the nearby woods to make sure that this incident cannot be traced back to you.

The Aztec warriors are well trained and equipped, and in short order you are driven from the farms. As soon as you sound the retreat, the Aztecs turn their attention to the farms. They work quickly and somehow manage to put out the fire before it spread to most of the crops.
Continue.

Though you have burnt down the farm houses, the Aztecs will easily be able to return and harvest the crops. For your attack to have any sort of effect, you need to kill those warriors and burn the crops.
Leave.
Gutiérrez's Cannon

You're moving along the bottom of a ravine when you come across a chilling sight. You stop to ponder the implications of what you've found, and your people gather around you, gazing silently at the sight before you. Along the small creek lazily making its way through the ravine are several scattered skeletons unmistakably clad in the armour of Spanish soldiers.
Investigate the scene

A remarkable amount of arrows are stuck in the surrounding trees and undergrowth, all at angles that indicate they were fired from the cliffs above. A half-broken light cannon lies abandoned along the riverbed, together with several equine skeletons and their still-full saddlebags. It's obvious that if anyone survived this ambush, they must have fled the area with arrows still raining down from above.
Examine the arrows.

There is nothing particularly suspicious about the arrows in and of themselves. Indeed, they appear to be typical Aztec arrows used mainly for hunting. It does strike you, however, that there are far fewer arrows to be found than you would expect from a scene like this.
Continue.

Looking around for marks where arrows may have struck and later been reclaimed, you are surprised and confused to instead find holes where arquebus bullets have dug themselves into the trees. Whoever ambushed these soldiers were partially armed with Spanish weapons.
Examine the cannon.

Your people peel the encrusted mud off the sides of the cannon and drag it out of the river. It appears to miraculously still be in working order. FName1 lets out a grunt when FHeShe1 sees the engravings along its barrel.

"Capitán, I've seen this cannon before. This is the Falconet that was given to Felipe Gutiérrez by His Majesty the King! It was given during a ceremony in Madrid before Gutiérrez embarked on his expedition."
"I'm not surprised. Who other than Gutiérrez could have brought a cannon here?"
"Yes, but... for Gutiérrez to leave this gift behind and not come back for it, he and his men must have been in grave danger indeed."
"Furthermore, why did his attackers not take it?"
FNameFirst1 nods gravely.
Take the cannon.

Your people haul the broken cannon onto one of your carts. You'll have to assign somebody to repair it when you make camp. Your people also find a few shots of ammunition and gunpowder for your new weapon. Then you bury the skeletons along with their rusted weapons and armour.
Leave.
You move on along the ravine, carefully watching the cliffs above. On the way, you notice heavy footprints preserved in the mud. Could it be that anybody survived this ambush?
Leave.
Gutiérrez's Cross

Your expedition is carefully making its way up a narrow path on the side of a mountain when you turn a corner to be faced with a beautiful view. Rose-coloured clouds stretch across the sky and reflect the sun's light across the lush landscape far below you. A single sturdy tree, timelessly ancient, makes a striking silhouette at the top of a rock outcropping. Beneath its canopy stands a solitary wooden cross.
Examine the cross.
The side of the cross facing away from the cliff is engraved with the outlines of a flower and nothing more. Into the backside the following inscription has been artfully carved:
"Sweet Mountain Flower. Justice Will Be Done."
Continue.
At the foot of the cross, arranged to face away from the cross and towards the horizon, is an exquisite conquistador's helmet engraved with a gold pattern.
Examine the helmet.

You recognise the helmet as soon as you pick it up: it belonged to the conquistador Felipe Gutiérrez, who was sent on an expedition three years prior to yours, from which nobody ever returned. Beneath the helmet is a small, distinctly feminine pouch full of medicinal herbs and remedies. The name "Ines" is stitched into it.
Continue.
FName1 leans forward.
"That helmet looks valuable... I'm just putting it out there."
Continue.
From behind FHimHer1, FName2 raises FHisHer2 hands in warning.
"This site is a memorial for somebody who fell in service to the Spanish crown. Taking the helmet is the equivalent of disturbing the grave of a Christian."
Continue.
From behind FHimHer1, FName2 grumbles disapprovingly.
"You better not be suggesting what I think you're suggesting. Felipe Gutiérrez was a hero, he left his helmet here for a reason."
Continue.
FName1 leans forward.
"This site is a memorial for somebody who fell in service to the Spanish crown. Hopefully I need not remind anyone here that taking the helmet would be the equivalent of disturbing a grave."
Continue.
FName1 leans forward.
"Felipe Gutiérrez was a hero, he left his helmet here for a reason. We must leave it here, where he intended."
Continue.
FName raises FHisHer hand from the back.
"Capitán, if I may. Regardless of Gutiérrez's intentions, the dead do not need armour - the living do. A lot of care went into the making of this helmet, it might save one of our lives some day."
Take the medicine and the helmet.
You elect to take both the medicine and the helmet with you, but leave the empty pouch at the foot of the cross.
Leave the helmet, take the medicine.
You elect to take the medicine with you, but leave the pouch beneath the helmet at the foot of the cross, just as you found it.
Leave.
Gutiérrez's Hunting Camp

You've been engaged in an arduous struggle against the vines and undergrowth of the wilderness for many hours when you finally approach a clearing in the jungle. From a distance you can make out wooden posts that might be part of a tribal village, but to your surprise you find traces of a hunting camp typical of the Spanish military.
Investigate the camp.

Judging from the arrangement of what traces remain, it must have been slightly more than just an overnight camp. Trees have been felled to make crude barricades and boardwalks of their wood, and traces still remain in the ground where tents were erected.
Continue.
In the underbrush near the outskirts of the clearing, FName1 spots something glimmering and brings it to you. It's a golden locket inlaid with precious gems, clearly created in Spain.
Open the locket.

The locket is slightly hard to open after spending a long time in the damp jungle, but eventually you pry it up. It contains a picture of a very beautiful young woman with the inscription "To my dear Inés. Forever yours. Felipe."
"You found it, FNameFirst1. Keep it."
FNameFirst1 gives you a puzzled smile.
"Gracias, Capitán. I'll keep it safe."
Take the locket.
You decide to bring the locket with you, if nothing else than to return it to Doña Inés' family back in Spain.
Leave.
Gutiérrez's Revenge

Returning to the abandoned settlement on the river bank, you get the same sense of quiet foreboding as last time you were here. The Spanish fortifications have not been touched since your last visit, and broken weapons and equipment still litter the ground. Some of the huts still have pots of preserved food. The settlement is flanked on either side by what appears to be graveyards.

While walking along the river, you spot the huts of a small Aztec village on the bank up ahead. You approach the village with caution, but as you come closer, you see that the huts have been burned and no living soul appears to be present.
Enter the village.

Upon entering the village, you find that a hasty palisade has been erected along the side of the town facing away from the river. Trampled tents unmistakably belonging to the Spanish military lie scattered along the fortifications, and broken weapons and equipment litter the ground. Some of the huts still have pots of preserved food. The settlement is flanked on either side by what appears to be graveyards.
Continue.
FName1 shudders.
"I have a bad feeling about this, Capitán."
Assign an expedition member as look-out.
You order FName to keep watch outside the abandoned village and sound the alarm if FHeShe1 spots anything suspicious.
"Sí Capitán, I'll keep an eye out for trouble."
Investigate the huts.

Your people systematically check the jars in each hut and supplement your expedition's food stores with anything sufficiently preserved. Most of the food appears to have been inedible for many months, but a few of the pots contain consumables it wouldn't kill you to eat (yet). The largest of the huts has no food, but contains an interesting scrap of paper that somebody must have dropped during the fighting.
Examine the paper.
Gutiérrez's Fate
Follow the river south-west to locate the depot used by Gutiérrez's expedition.

It's a neatly folded note written in Spanish that says: "I am adjusting our plans. If we are unable to regroup after bringing the betrayer to justice, follow the river south-west to the old gate and wait by our depot. If we get there first, we will do the same. If the natives are restless, the supplies will easily keep us alive for a few days until it is safe to start our journey back to the ships." The note is signed with the seal of Felipe Gutiérrez.
Investigate the palisades.

The palisades are visibly deteriorated and must have stood unmaintained for at least a year, but they clearly weren't very impressive to begin with. They do appear to have been Spanish-made, as they don't resemble anything you've seen the Aztec construct. You note that there are bullet holes in some of the wood facing away from the village, which suggests that the attackers were Spanish or at least armed with European weapons.
Investigate the graveyard.

Both graveyards are placed so close to the town that you presume whoever created them knew nobody was going to live in the town anymore. One graveyard has a score of primitive wooden crosses arranged into three uneven rows, the other consists of about twice as many similar crosses. Some of the crosses in the smaller graveyard have Spanish hats and keepsakes hanging from them, whereas the crosses in the larger set are unadorned, but clearly both graveyards must have been created by Christians.
Leave.
Leave.
You're finishing up when your lookout FNameFirst1 comes sprinting into the abandoned settlement.
"Friends! Capitán! The locals are coming, they're going to attack!"
"How long?"
"Ten minutes at most, we have to get ready! And Capitán... they are led by two Spaniards!"
"Are you sure their intentions are hostile?"
"Trust me Capitán, /very/ hostile indeed. And Capitán... they are led by Spaniards!"
Prepare for battle.

You're finishing up when your lookout FNameFirst1 comes sprinting into the abandoned settlement, an arrow quite conspicuously protruding from FHisHer1 shoulder, screaming at the top of FHisHer1 lungs.
"Friends! Capitán! Help! We're under attack, they took me by surprise!"
Continue.

FNameFirst1 is immediately followed by a group of natives, clearly armed and prepared to fight. Even more shockingly, your eyes are caught by the sun reflecting off a steel breastplate: two Spaniards are leading the charge!

You're finishing up when - much to everybody's surprise - a group of natives bursts out of the wilderness, clearly armed and prepared to fight. Even more shockingly, your eyes are caught by the sun reflecting off a steel breastplate: two Spaniards are leading the charge!
"To arms!"
Victorious, you and your people regain your composures and check on each other and the enemies. All the attackers are either dead or dying, and sadly the Spaniards are among the former.
Continue.

Examining their belongings, it's clear that they were subordinates of Felipe Gutiérrez, though you have no way to say what side they fought on when that expedition apparently turned on itself. You add their weapons and trinkets to your stores and move on.

Defeated, you and your expedition members are chased out of the settlement and most of the way back towards your caravan. Mercifully, you lose your pursuers just before you rejoin your servants. Everybody seems to have made it out alive.
Continue.

As you prepare to put this latest defeat behind you and move out, there's a lot of murmurings among the troops, exchanging theories in hushed tones as to the nature of the Spaniards who just led a group of savages to attack you.
Avoid the village.
Gutiérrez's Treasure

Making your way slowly up the river, your people seem a little on edge. Perhaps it's excitement about the possibility of finding some of their long lost countrymen alive; perhaps it's quiet dread at the prospect of discovering the demise of Felipe Gutiérrez. Most likely it's a mix of both.
Continue.

You're keeping an eye out for anything that could be described as "the gate", and eventually a pretty promising candidate shows up among the tree tops a little ways into the jungle: a giant stone arch that looks like it ought to be the entrance to an enormous temple, but which seems to be standing all alone between the trees.
Approach the arch.

You leave your horses with the servants and take your followers to investigate the arch. The arch itself is uncharacteristically plain, hewn from rough stones as though whoever erected it somehow never got around to etching in the typical Aztec symbols that you've seen many times on your travels. You pass through it without incident and stop to survey the ruins of the modest buildings on the other side. Far from an enormous palace deserving of such an imposing gateway, three small stone houses is all you find.
Search the houses.
Gutiérrez's Fate

Inside one of the houses, you find what must be the remains of Felipe Gutiérrez. A skeleton sitting on the floor, propped up against the old stone wall, clothed in the withered remains of once fine garbs, bones long since picked clean by whatever vermin lives in this part of the jungle. Old traces of blood on the floor illustrate his path towards what became his final resting place. Next to his hand lies his beautiful banner with his family crest. His other hand clutches a piece of cloth, part of the uniform of an officer of the Spanish navy. It is soaked in dried-up blood.
Search the other houses.

The other houses contain a great amount of goods that must make up the spoils of Gutiérrez's expedition: Fine Aztec works of art, most of it made out of gold or coated in it. Sacks that look like they used to contain several days worth of rations which have since been eaten by vermin. A few securely packed boxes of medicinal supplies partly from Spain but supplemented with native remedies. The only thing missing is weapons.
Continue.
You send somebody back to get the horses and salvage everything that's salvageable. Before you leave, you're compelled to give Gutiérrez a proper burial.
Continue.
FName picks Gutiérrez's banner up off the ground and raises it, admiring it as it unfolds.
"This is a beautiful banner. He would want to be buried with it."
Continue.
FName folds FHisHer hands respectfully in front of FHimHer.
"I think it would be a disgrace to bury Gutiérrez's banner, FNameFirst1. We should take it with us and bring it into battle - as it was meant to be used - in honour of his memory."
Keep the banner and bury Gutiérrez without it.
Disapproving murmurs pass between some members of your expedition when your servants cover the fresh grave of Gutiérrez with dirt.
Continue.

The murmurs quiet down as they place a wooden cross, as nice as you had time to make it, on the great explorer's grave. But when you carefully pack his banner in amongst your belongings and head out again, the sense of disapproval lingers in the air like a stench of rotten garbage.
Bury Gutiérrez with his banner.

You respectfully place Gutiérrez's banner next to his bones before your servants fill his grave with dirt. All the members of your expedition form a respectful circle around the site when the wooden cross, as nice as you had time to make it, is placed on the great explorer's grave.
Continue.
You all help pack the medicine and valuables from the dead man's expedition in amongst your own cargo and quietly set out to continue your own adventures.
Leave.
Causeway

A group of Aztec warriors has already assembled to bait the Totonac into attacking on your orders. The causeways are excellent chokepoints that make Tenochtitlan highly defendable, but the attacking army is so great in number that you can already tell you won't be able to hold them back for long.
Continue.

In the city behind you, the bulk of the Aztec army is still in the finishing stages of their battle preparations, so if you can just prevent the initial assault from breaking through your lines, you'll be able to safely fall back into the city and find another place to make your small but well equipped force useful.
[Check Tactics Medium] Attempt to collapse half the causeway.

You manage to identify the posts that need to be destroyed in order to collapse a strategically significant part of the causeways, and a few of your servants run out on the earthen bridge to chip away at them with their axes. When the poles are just about to give way, your servants tie ropes around them and scramble back to terra firma, handing the other ends to you.

You attempt to identify the posts that need to be destroyed in order to collapse a strategically significant part of the causeways, and a few of your servants run out on the earthen bridge to chip away at them with their axes. The poles give way sooner than expected, and your servants scramble back to terra firma. Unfortunately it doesn't have the desired effect, and the collapse probably won't make much of a difference in the battle.
Give the word to bait the Totonac.

A smaller group of Aztec warriors emit a war cry and charge down the causeway towards the Totonac encampments. A small skirmish ensues, and about half the baiters make it back across the causeway in one piece. Behind them, a Totonac advance group forms up and prepares to assault the causeway.
Continue.
A lone figure appears in front of the Totonac advance group, and shouts your name.
"PNAME! PNAME!"
Continue.
Miguel Sicart covers his mouth with his hands.
"Oh no... Ana!"
Continue.

You barely recognise Anacaona at the other end of the earthen bridge. Her face is covered in war paint, her simple gown has been replaced with a less restrictive outfit, and her pose is fierce and confrontational.

"My father has honoured his oath and the warriors of Xalapa remain in Xalapa like good little subjects to our /great/ and /merciful/ emperor Moctezuma! I've made no such oath so I have taken my father's place here to ensure that you're brought to justice!"
"Does your father even know that you're here?"
She shakes her fist angrily, but her small size makes it seem almost comical.

"My father the chieftain ought to be much less concerned with my well-being and more concerned with the war he's set in motion! Look out across the assembled Totonac armies look at how many people have come here to fight only to be deserted at the last moment by the man who brought them all here! You forced my father to betray his people and I am here to right that wrong!"
Continue.
From the roar of approval that rings out behind her, you'd think she was addressing her troops rather than you.
"You're no warrior, Ana! Go home and leave the fighting to the grown-ups!"
"Stay out of this! I don't want to have to hurt you!"
"You're no warrior, Ana! Go home and leave the fighting to the grown-ups!"
She raises her bow and waves it triumphantly over her head. Most of the warriors behind her do likewise.
"I /am/ grown up now PNameFirst! Thanks to /you/ I have seen what people are made of and now you have to face what you've created!"
"Stay out of this! I don't want to have to hurt you!"
She bends over forwards, and though it's hard to make out, you think she's laughing mockingly at you. You're being mocked by a little girl.
"BUT I /DO/ WANT TO HURT YOU, PNAMEFIRST! FOR MY FATHER!"

She turns around and signals for the attack to begin, and astoundingly, the Totonac warriors move forward with grim determination, as though ordered to advance by a legendary general. The small girl is disappears among her own subordinates, and your men steel themselves against the assault.
Tepictoton steps ahead of the Totonac warriors onto the end of the earthen bridge. He wears the outfit of a Jaguar Warrior and holds a spear high above his head.
"Cunning move, Spaniard, to attack Xalapa when I was away and had brought my most elite warriors with me! And what did I find when I arrived at Papantla, if not a smoldering ruin!"
Continue.

"Papantla, too, was far too much for you to handle without cheap tricks, is that not right? It was /you/ who poisoned their water ahead of the attack, reducing their army to a mere shadow of what it should be!"
Continue.
"Well this time you have to face me, and the full force of the assembled Totonac army! You have no more tricks or deceptions left! Finally we will see how you will manage in a real battle!"

"You have a talent for ruthlessness, Spaniard! Just like your predecessor! Xalapa's army may be defeated, but Aztec allies or no, you will never be able to withstand the assembled armies of the Totonac!"
"How in God's name are you still alive? Didn't we already kill you?"
"With the help of the gods, I lived to fight another day - and today is that day, PName!"

"You dare ask that of me, PName? You, who have crossed the ocean to interfere in matters that ought not concern you? You, who have brought iron-clad soldiers to our lands to wrest control of it from our hands?!"

Continue.

Tepictoton turns around and signals for the attack to begin, and the Totonac warriors raise their weapons and charge down the causeway towards your position. The chieftain is swallowed up in his subordinates, and your men steel themselves against the assault.

"The Totonac have crossed the lake in their canoes, an advance group have captured the military district! You have to bring your men in there and take that district back, we'll hold the causeway and buy you time!"
"How could they take the military district?!"

"It was held by a skeleton crew, the bulk of our forces were defending the causeways!"
"We'll recapture it!"
"We will crush them."
"I will, good luck!"

"The Tlaxcalteca and the Totonac have crossed the lake in their canoes! Tlaxcala has wrestled control of the market from our warriors while the Totonac invaded the military district. You have to bring your men in there and take these districts back, we'll hold the causeway and buy you time!"

"It is over. My forces... crushed. The Totonac, they have the milit-- litary district. They crossed the lake... in their canoes."

Unbelievably, Quappiatl /chuckles/.
"I believe the war... is lost. If you disagree... take your troops to the military district. Throw out the Totonac. Take it /back/."

The tactical situation on the causeway remains unchanged - the Aztec defenders are well dug in and will take a concerted effort to unseat from their positions along the earthen bridge. You are led to Tepictoton, who stands on a hill near the lakeside, scouting across the lake with a hand shading his eyes. As soon as you reach him, he speaks to you without turning.
"I have long imagined standing in this very spot, overlooking this magnificent city. I never dreamed it would happen so soon, however - this is all thanks to you, PName."
"How fares the war?"
He finally lowers his hand and turns to face you. He looks slightly overwhelmed by emotion.
"Thousands have died on Lake Texcoco. We sent our canoes, they sent theirs. The island is impenetrable, we will never break through their defences on the causeways."

"Your troops, yes - that is my hope. Once the causeway is broken, we stand a chance, but it will still be a difficult battle."
Continue.

"The Tlaxcalteca have reinforced the Aztecs on the island, they seem to have arrived here a day before we did. Tlaxcala's warriors are fierce, they have resisted the Aztec Empire for years - whatever their task in the city, their group will be a great hurdle to our victory."
Continue.

"Of course, the Aztec elite will be defending Moctezuma's palace. I am not confident that my own warriors can stand against all the Eagle Warriors of Tenochtitlan, but you might have a chance. We must get to the Tlatoani at all costs - as long as he lives, Tenochtitlan will stand."
"It will be my pleasure to aid you by killing Moctezuma."

Patli examines the body in detail, ignoring the putrid smell. Never have you seen a man so unmoved by the grotesque. He takes a small knife and carefully cuts off several of the boils on the body. Patli acknowledges you with a small nod and digs back into the corpse. A few minutes later, he exhumes the heart and places it gently in a small bowl, which he then covers with a small piece of cloth and stows away in a basket in the corner.

Patli shrugs and digs back into the corpse. A few minutes later, he exhumes the heart and places it gently in a small bowl, which he then covers with a small piece of cloth and stows away in a basket in the corner.
